title: Legacy CRM Recipe Apps — Account Management Modules (Account Team, Next Best Customer, Territory Dashboard)
summary: Detailed operational architecture of the account management module cluster in a legacy life sciences CRM, covering Account Team cross-functional visibility, Next Best Customer algorithmic prioritization, and Territory Status Dashboard performance visualization across device form factors.

findings.account_team_widget: The Account Team widget displays the cross-functional team assigned to an account with role-based member visibility. Supported on iPad and Web in offline-capable mode. Each team member entry shows role, contact details, and relationship context. The widget renders within existing account profile pages as an embeddable section, enabling field representatives to quickly identify the relevant contacts for a given account without navigating to a separate screen.
findings.next_best_customer_widget: The Next Best Customer widget uses algorithmic scoring to recommend which accounts to prioritize for engagement. Supported on all five device types (iPad, iPhone, Web, Android Tablet, Android Phone) in online-only mode. The scoring model considers call history, plan cycle targets, product alignment, and territory coverage gaps. The widget surfaces a ranked list of accounts with the recommendation rationale, enabling representatives to optimize their visit schedules based on data-driven prioritization rather than manual planning.
findings.territory_status_dashboard: The Territory Status Dashboard widget provides territory-level performance metrics and KPI visualization. Supported on all five device types in online-only mode. The dashboard aggregates data across all accounts within the representative's territory assignment, presenting summary metrics for visit completion, product coverage, and engagement trends. The visualization uses chart-based rendering with drill-down capability to individual account performance.
findings.device_support_patterns: Account Team follows the Tier 3 pattern (iPad and Web only), reflecting its use primarily in office and planning contexts. Next Best Customer and Territory Status Dashboard follow the Tier 1 pattern (all five devices), enabling field access on any device. All three widgets are online-only except Account Team, which supports offline access through locally synchronized team assignment data.

title: Legacy CRM Recipe Apps — Planning and Execution Modules (Activity Plans, Plan Cycle, Approvals, Call To Dos)
summary: Detailed operational architecture of the planning and execution module cluster in a legacy life sciences CRM, covering Activity Plan Completion Reports with variance analysis, Plan Cycle Summary aggregation, Approval Requests workflow queues, Call Details History, and Call To Dos follow-up tracking.

findings.activity_plan_completion_report: The Activity Plan Completion Report is a full-screen app supported on all five device types in online-only mode. It tracks field execution against cyclical visit plans with completion percentages and variance analysis. The report shows planned versus actual visit counts per account, product discussion targets versus delivered, and overall plan cycle adherence. Representatives and managers use this to identify accounts that are behind schedule and need prioritized attention. The report supports filtering by account segment, product group, and time period within the active plan cycle.
findings.plan_cycle_summary_widget: The Plan Cycle Summary widget aggregates plan cycle performance across accounts, products, and representatives. Supported on iPad and Web in offline-capable mode. The widget presents a consolidated view of how the current planning period is tracking, including total calls completed versus target, product coverage gaps, and representative ranking within the territory hierarchy. Offline capability means representatives can review their plan progress during field visits without network connectivity.
findings.approval_requests_app: The Approval Requests app provides a unified queue for pending approval workflows across multiple business processes. Supported on iPad, iPhone, and Web in online-only mode. The queue consolidates approval requests from different functional areas (time-off-territory requests, data change requests, expense approvals, and business plan modifications) into a single actionable interface. Managers can review, approve, or reject requests with comments directly from the queue without navigating to each originating record.
findings.call_details_and_todos: Call Details History is a widget displaying historical visit records with product discussions, key messages delivered, and outcomes. Supported on iPad, iPhone, and Web in offline-capable mode. Call To Dos is a companion widget surfacing pending post-call action items and follow-up tasks. Both widgets render within account and call context pages, providing representatives with a complete view of past interactions and outstanding commitments for any given account. Offline capability ensures access to historical call data during field visits.
findings.call_history_integration: The Call Details History widget supports filtering by call type, date range, and product discussed. Each call record entry shows the call date, attendees, products detailed, key messages delivered, samples disbursed, and any post-call notes. The widget integrates with the Call To Dos widget — completing a todo automatically updates the associated call record's follow-up status, maintaining a closed-loop tracking system between visit execution and post-visit commitments.

title: Legacy CRM Recipe Apps — Meeting and Event Management Modules (Budgets, Pulse, Sign In Sheet, Speakers, Topics)
summary: Detailed operational architecture of the meeting and event management module cluster in a legacy life sciences CRM, covering five interconnected sub-modules that manage the complete lifecycle of scientific meetings from budget allocation through attendee tracking and post-event analysis.

findings.meeting_budgets_widget: The Meeting Budgets widget tracks financial allocation and consumption for scientific meetings and events. It displays system-generated budget filters matched to specific meetings, showing allocated amounts, committed spend, and remaining budget in real-time. The consumption tracking model links individual expense line items (venue, catering, speaker fees, materials) to the parent budget, enabling meeting organizers to monitor spend against allocation. Budget matching uses record type and meeting classification to automatically associate the correct budget pool.
findings.meeting_pulse_widget: The Meeting Pulse widget provides real-time event engagement metrics during live meetings. The dashboard displays: attendee count and status (registered, checked-in, absent), countdown timer to meeting start or end, outstanding sample requests from attendees, estimated total meeting cost (dynamically calculated from confirmed attendees and per-person cost factors), and recent inquiries and insights submitted during the event. This widget serves as the meeting coordinator's primary operational view during event execution.
findings.meeting_sign_in_sheet: The Meeting Sign In Sheet widget captures attendee presence through signature collection. Features include: electronic signature capture on the device screen, record type filtering to segment attendees by role or organization type, meal tracking to record which attendees received meals (relevant for compliance reporting), and write-in attendee support for unregistered walk-in participants. The signature data is stored as part of the attendance record, creating an auditable proof of attendance for regulatory compliance with healthcare event reporting requirements.
findings.meeting_speakers_widget: The Meeting Speakers widget manages speaker program assignments for scientific meetings. It includes a preferred country default filter sourced from master data management records, enabling automatic filtering of the speaker pool based on the meeting location and regulatory jurisdiction. Speaker assignments link to the meeting record and track speaker credentials, topic assignments, and compensation terms. The integration with external reference data ensures speaker recommendations align with the geographic and specialty requirements of each event.
findings.meeting_topics_widget: The Meeting Topics widget manages the scientific agenda for meetings. Topics are filtered by approved topic status, meeting record type and subtype, and date validity period. This filtering ensures that only currently approved scientific content topics are available for selection, enforcing medical-legal-regulatory compliance. The topic approval workflow ensures that all meeting content has been reviewed and approved before it can be presented, creating a compliant content governance chain for scientific exchange events.

title: Legacy CRM Recipe Apps — Data, Compliance, and Samples Modules (OneKey, EPPV/MID, Orders, Samples Management)
summary: Detailed operational architecture of the data enrichment, regulatory compliance, order management, and sample distribution modules in a legacy life sciences CRM, covering reference data validation, compliance tracking workflows, order fulfillment, and the complete sample inventory lifecycle with seven distinct sub-sections.

findings.onekey_accelerated_insights: The Accelerated Insights module consolidates digital and scientific insights from an external healthcare provider network. It aggregates social media presence data, publication history, and clinical trial participation into a single view per provider account. This enables representatives to prepare for interactions with current context about the provider's recent scientific activity and public engagement. Supported on iPad and Web in online-only mode, as the data requires real-time retrieval from the external provider network.
findings.onekey_validation_request: The Validation Request module enables field-initiated data correction requests for provider and organization records. Two record types are supported: Workplace (address and affiliation updates) and Activity (account status and specialty updates). Representatives submit validation requests when they identify incorrect or outdated information during field visits, routing the correction through a defined approval workflow before the master data is updated. This creates a governed data quality process where field observations feed back into the reference data system.
findings.eppv_mid_compliances: The EPPV (Educational Programs and Professional Visits) and MID (Medical Information Disclosures) Compliances widget tracks regulatory compliance requirements for healthcare professional interactions. The module operates on a cycle-based tracking model where compliance todos are generated per account per cycle period. Survey types include Face to Face, Direct Mail, Phone, Fax, and Email interactions. At the call level, a dedicated EPPV/MID tab allows representatives to record compliance activities linked to the visit. iPhone display is limited to three columns. Once a call is submitted, EPPV/MID entries cannot be modified, enforcing an immutable audit trail for compliance records.
findings.orders_and_deliveries: The Orders module includes two sub-components: Deliveries (widget showing the last 30 days plus future scheduled deliveries, filterable by account, product, and brand) and Search for Orders (widget with comprehensive filtering by order name, product name, date ranges, order status, delivery status, and brand). Order creation is available as a Quick Action from Call and Meeting contexts. The order workflow supports Save as In Progress for draft orders and Submit for completed orders, with product selection from the authorized product catalog and quantity entry with allocation validation.
findings.samples_management_architecture: The Samples Management module is the most complex recipe app, spanning both widget and full-screen app variants with seven distinct functional areas: (1) Disbursements Chart — visual summary of sample disbursement activity over 3, 6, or 12 month periods, showing distribution trends by product. (2) Inventories — supports four inventory types (Initial, Ad Hoc, Periodic, and Audited), each with physical count reconciliation against system counts. When an inventory is submitted, the system automatically creates adjustment records to reconcile differences between physical and system counts. (3) Manage Lots — lot lifecycle management with Active/Inactive toggle, tracking lot numbers, expiration dates, and availability status. (4) Received Samples — tracks inbound sample shipments including Acknowledgment of Shipment and Transfer In records, with Acknowledge, Return to Sender, and Duplicate actions for each pending receipt. (5) Sample Storage Locations — configurable storage addresses with default location selection for shipment routing. (6) Samples Timeline — comprehensive chronological view of all sample transactions (disbursements, orders, transfers, adjustments) and orders in a unified timeline filterable by All, Transactions, or Orders. (7) Reconciliation Report — displays sample request quotas by account/specialty/template/period with disbursed and remaining quantities in a donut chart visualization.
findings.sample_transactions_detail: Six sample transaction types are supported, each with distinct form layouts: Transfer Out (recipient rep, territory, ship-to address, shipment date/carrier/tracking), Acknowledgment of Shipment (received date, condition of package as Undamaged/Damaged/Opened), Adjustment (quantity as positive for increase or negative for decrease, reason as Theft/Loss, Incorrect Disbursement, or Other), Return (shipment date, carrier, tracking number for returning samples to the company), Transfer In (from sales rep, ship-to address, received date, condition of package), and Order (ship-to address, urgency flag, product grid with quantity and remaining allocation). All transactions follow a Save/Submit lifecycle where Save creates an In Progress draft and Submit finalizes the record.

title: Legacy CRM Recipe Apps — Engagement Modules (Remote Sessions, Sales Analytics, Content Library, Quick Actions)
summary: Detailed operational architecture of the engagement and productivity module cluster in a legacy life sciences CRM, covering remote digital detailing sessions, sales performance visualization, offline-capable content access, and configurable shortcut actions for field execution efficiency.

findings.remote_engagements_app: The Remote Engagements module includes a Launch Remote Session widget that displays scheduled calls and meetings for the current day, filtered by account when accessed from a profile screen. The module supports video and digital detailing sessions with integrated content presentation capabilities. Supported on iPad and Web in online-only mode, as remote sessions require real-time network connectivity for video streaming and content synchronization. The widget serves as the entry point for virtual interactions, bridging the gap between in-person field visits and digital engagement channels.
findings.sales_chart_widget: The Sales Chart widget provides dual-view analytics: a Sales Chart displaying market and product performance data, and a Calls Per Month chart segmented by call type. The widget supports both territory-level aggregation (showing all accounts within the representative's territory) and account-level drill-down (showing performance for a specific account). Supported on all five device types (iPad, iPhone, Web, Android Tablet, Android Phone) in online-only mode. The dual-view design enables representatives to correlate their call activity patterns with sales outcomes, identifying whether increased engagement with specific accounts or product segments translates to measurable performance changes.
findings.content_library_widget: The Content Library widget provides access to approved marketing materials by allowing representatives to attach files from the platform's content management system to records such as accounts, calls, and meetings. The widget operates in both online and offline modes — content is synchronized to the device during sync cycles, with sync indicators showing the download status of each asset. Supported on iPad, iPhone, and Web. The offline capability is critical for field representatives who need to access and share approved clinical documents, product information sheets, and marketing collateral during visits in locations with limited or no network connectivity.
findings.quick_actions_widget: The Quick Actions widget provides configurable shortcut buttons for frequently used operations during field visits. Supported actions include creating Orders, Inquiries, and Store Checks directly from Call or Meeting contexts. On iPad and Web, all action types are available. On iPhone, the action set is limited to Create Call from the Meetings screen. Quick Actions eliminate navigation steps by allowing representatives to trigger common workflows from their current context — for example, creating an inquiry about a product directly from within an active call record without navigating away from the visit documentation screen. The widget is configurable by administrators to include custom actions beyond the built-in set.
